title: Coordinate boundary geometric pullback in Gysin charts
statement:
The actual coordinate support boundary pulls back to the fibre coordinate boundary,
for any two snake-normalized Gysin charts. This is an equality of support classes,
independent of a global orientation morphism or any residue isomorphism.

Its exact Lean specification is: theorem orientation_coordinate_boundary_pullback (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) (h : P.ramificationIndex ∣ P.level) (Y : Scheme.{u}) (a : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) [IsSeparated a] [LocallyOfFiniteType a] [QuasiCompact a] (D : OrientationSupportData P h Y) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] [Algebra P.field.k Ω] (y : Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (hy : y ≫ a = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.field.k Ω))) (D' : OrientationSupportData P h (Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω))) : ∃ p : proEtaleSupportHomTransport P (zeroSection Y) (zeroSection (Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω))) (AffineSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) y), P.orientationSupportRestriction h y p (D.coordinateBoundary P h a) = D'.coordinateBoundary P h (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.field.k Ω)))

Notions: [def-pur-conventions], [def-pur-affine-line-datum], [def-pur-orientation-support-data].

proof.text: Use choice projections of coordinate_boundary_geometric_pullback to obtain only its normalized models M and Mprime, transport p, and pro-etale coefficient-compatible equality. The orientation support restriction unfolds in one step to coefficientGroupMap of coordinateProCoefficientPullback, so the supplied equality has exactly the needed type. Apply orientation_coordinate_model_boundary to both charts, compose these equalities, and rewrite y followed by a using the k-morphism equation.
